page: Microsoft Azure D8plds_v7 is an ARM64 virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware specification includes 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, does not contain discrete GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The 1:2 memory-to-core allocation provides an efficient resource profile for compute-oriented workloads where extensive memory capacity is unnecessary. By pairing 8 dedicated ARM cores with a modest memory footprint, the instance optimizes hardware resource efficiency. The bundled 472 GB local NVMe SSD offers high-speed temporary storage suitable for caching and fast IOPS, though users must account for the architectural requirements of the ARM64 instruction set.

The D8plds_v7 instance is targeted at software compile tasks, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, batch execution routines, web servers, and containerized microservices compiled natively for ARM64 environments.
